'''Felix Kolmer''' (3 May 1922 – 5 August 2022) was a Czech Holocaust survivor and physicist, specialising in the field of [[acoustics]]. During the [[World War II|Second World War]], he was active in the [[Resistance in the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia|Czech Resistance]].

== Early life ==
Kolmer was born in Prague in 1922 to an assimilated Jewish family. His father died in 1932, and he subsequently spent holidays in Austria with his uncle.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skautskyinstitut.cz/stories/prof-ing-drsc-felix-kolmer-1922/|title=Prof. Ing., DrSc. Felix Kolmer (1922)|work=Skautsky institut|access-date=24 July 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=19 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719173837/https://www.skautskyinstitut.cz/stories/prof-ing-drsc-felix-kolmer-1922/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a result, he was in Austria during the 1938–1945 [[Occupation of Czechoslovakia (1938–1945)|Nazi invasion and occupation of Czechoslovakia]].

== In Terezín ==
Kolmer was selected to be part of the ''Aufbaukommando'', the first transportation to [[Theresienstadt Ghetto|Terezín]]. The transport contained young able-bodied Jewish men, with the intention that the men would assist in building the ghetto.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.holocaust.cz/dejiny/udalosti/aufbaukommando-1941/|title=Aufbaukommando (1941)|website=Holocaust|language=cs|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> In Terezín, he was specifically forced to build bunk beds, since he had carpentry experience.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://zpravy.idnes.cz/rozhovor-s-felixem-kolmerem-d1y-/domaci.aspx?c=A150116_080409_domaci_jw|title=V tom místě nešlo počítat dny, vzpomíná český uprchlík z Osvětimi|date=18 January 2015|website=iDNES.cz|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> At one point, he was interned in the Small Fortress, and the treatment of prisoners by the SS that he witnessed there prompted him to join the underground resistance.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.memoryofnations.eu/en/kolmer-felix-1922|title=Felix Kolmer (1922) – Biography|website=Memory of Nations|access-date=11 April 2021}}</ref> He found an escape route out of Terezín, but never used it; the route was used by a few prisoners later. He was able to use his ''Aufbaukommando'' status to temporarily protect some of his family members, including his grandmother, mother, and fiancée.<ref name=":0" /> His mother died in Terezín in 1941.

== Deportation to Auschwitz and escape ==
In October 1944, Kolmer was sent to [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz-Birkenau]]. According to his later recollections, he arrived on a transport with 1,500 people, 1,250 of whom were immediately sent to the gas chambers by [[Josef Mengele]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/1064884-felix-kolmer-aneb-smrt-v-usmevu-doktora-mengeleho|title=Felix Kolmer aneb Smrt v úsměvu doktora Mengeleho|publisher=Česká televize|work=ČT24|access-date=24 July 2018|language=cs}}</ref> Kolmer only survived this initial selection because a prisoner he did not know told the Nazis he was a metal worker.<ref name=":0" /> He managed to escape Auschwitz by jumping on a transport with a friend, which headed to the [[Gross-Rosen concentration camp|Gross-Rosen]] camp, specifically the subcamp Friedland.

== Later life ==
After the war, Kolmer worked as an electrical engineer,<ref name=":2" /> and became an expert on acoustics.<ref name=":1" /> Kolmer began lecturing not only in his field of expertise, but also on World War II.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kzt.famu.cz/pedagogove/prof-ing-felix-kolmer-drsc-2/|title=Prof. Ing. Felix Kolmer, DrSc.|website=Katedra zvukové tvorby|access-date=24 July 2018|archive-date=24 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724154309/http://kzt.famu.cz/pedagogove/prof-ing-felix-kolmer-drsc-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He received several awards for his resistance, scientific research, and bravery. He also assisted victims of the Nazis who are seeking compensation. He was interviewed by [[Post Bellum]], an oral history organisation, as part of their project ''Stories of the 20th Century''.

Kolmer [[Centenarian|turned 100]] in May 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://zoommagazin.iprima.cz/zajimavosti/felix-kolmer|title=Utekl ze tří koncentračních táborů a stal se vědeckou kapacitou. Felix Kolmer dnes slaví 100. narozeniny|publisher=Zoom magazin|date=3 May 2022|language=cs}}</ref> and died on 5 August.<ref>{{cite news |title=Holocaust survivor Felix Kolmer dies aged 100 |url=https://english.radio.cz/holocaust-survivor-felix-kolmer-dies-aged-100-8757898 |access-date=5 August 2022 |publisher=Radio Prague International |date=5 August 2022}}</ref>
